100: fn build_and_prepare(
101:     mutation: &SiteMutation,
102:     snapshot: &lifecycle::DeploymentSnapshot,
103:     context_dir: &Path,
104:     deployment: &mut release_state::DeploymentRecord,
105: ) -> Result<()> {
106:     if let Err(error) = lifecycle::checkout::run(snapshot, context_dir) {
107:         return finish_abort(mutation, Some(context_dir), error);
108:     }
109:     if let Err(error) =
110:         advance_phase(mutation, deployment, Some(release_state::DeploymentPhase::SourceExported), Some(context_dir))
111:     {
112:         return finish_abort(mutation, Some(context_dir), error);
113:     }
114: 
115:     stage("Building release");
116:     if let Err(error) = lifecycle::build::run(mutation, snapshot, context_dir) {
117:         return finish_abort(mutation, Some(context_dir), error);
118:     }
119:     if let Err(error) =
120:         advance_phase(mutation, deployment, Some(release_state::DeploymentPhase::Built), Some(context_dir))
121:     {
122:         return finish_abort(mutation, Some(context_dir), error);
123:     }
124: 
125:     stage("Preparing release");
126:     if let Err(error) = lifecycle::build::promote(mutation, snapshot, context_dir) {
127:         return finish_abort(mutation, Some(context_dir), error);
128:     }
129:     if let Err(error) =
130:         advance_phase(mutation, deployment, Some(release_state::DeploymentPhase::Promoted), Some(context_dir))
131:     {
132:         return finish_abort(mutation, Some(context_dir), error);
133:     }
134:     if let Err(error) = lifecycle::wire_shared::run(mutation, snapshot) {
135:         return finish_abort(mutation, Some(context_dir), error);
136:     }
137:     if let Err(error) = lifecycle::prepare::run(mutation, snapshot) {
138:         return finish_abort(mutation, Some(context_dir), error);
139:     }
140:     if let Err(error) =
141:         advance_phase(mutation, deployment, Some(release_state::DeploymentPhase::Prepared), Some(context_dir))
142:     {
143:         return finish_abort(mutation, Some(context_dir), error);
144:     }
145:     if let Err(error) = lifecycle::build::finalize(mutation, snapshot) {
146:         return finish_abort(mutation, Some(context_dir), error);
147:     }
148:     if let Err(error) =
149:         advance_phase(mutation, deployment, Some(release_state::DeploymentPhase::Sealed), Some(context_dir))
150:     {
151:         return finish_abort(mutation, Some(context_dir), error);
152:     }
153:     Ok(())
154: }
155: 
156: fn activate_deployment(mutation: &SiteMutation, prepared: &PreparedDeployment) -> Result<()> {
157:     // Phase B: cut-over — the commit point. Failure restores the previous
158:     // release (transactional rollback), leaving the site idle.
159:     stage("Activating release");
160:     if let Err(error) = lifecycle::activate::run(mutation, &prepared.snapshot) {
161:         return finish_abort(mutation, Some(&prepared.context_dir), error);
162:     }
163:     if let Err(error) = advance_phase(
164:         mutation,
165:         &prepared.deployment,
166:         Some(release_state::DeploymentPhase::Activated),
167:         Some(&prepared.context_dir),
168:     ) {
169:         return finish_abort(mutation, Some(&prepared.context_dir), error);
170:     }
171: 
172:     stage("Restarting services");
173:     if let Err(error) = service::run_for_release(mutation) {
174:         return finish_failed_activation(mutation, &prepared.previous_release, Some(&prepared.context_dir), error);
175:     }
176:     if let Err(error) = advance_phase(
177:         mutation,
178:         &prepared.deployment,
179:         Some(release_state::DeploymentPhase::Verified),
180:         Some(&prepared.context_dir),
181:     ) {
182:         return finish_abort_without_release_drop(mutation, Some(&prepared.context_dir), error);
183:     }
184:     Ok(())
185: }
186: 
187: fn complete_deployment(mutation: &SiteMutation, prepared: &PreparedDeployment) -> Result<()> {
188:     // Phase C: post-commit maintenance. The new release is serving; failures
189:     // here are recorded as `cleanup_pending` warnings, never deployment errors.
190:     if let Err(error) = run_maintenance(mutation, &prepared.context_dir) {
191:         finish_cleanup_pending(mutation, Some(&prepared.context_dir), &error);
192:         return Ok(());
193:     }
194:     if let Err(error) =
195:         advance_phase(mutation, &prepared.deployment, Some(release_state::DeploymentPhase::Completed), None)
196:     {
197:         finish_cleanup_pending(mutation, Some(&prepared.context_dir), &error);
198:         return Ok(());
199:     }
200:     mutation.clear_active()
201: }
202: 
203: /// Advances the persisted deployment phase and writes the record (with the
204: /// build context attached in Phase A). `phase` is `None` only for the initial
205: /// `created` write that records the context before the first transition.
206: fn advance_phase(
207:     mutation: &SiteMutation,
208:     deployment: &release_state::DeploymentRecord,
209:     phase: Option<release_state::DeploymentPhase>,
210:     context: Option<&Path>,
211: ) -> Result<()> {
212:     let mut record = deployment.clone();
213:     if let Some(phase) = phase {
214:         record.set_phase(phase);
215:     }
216:     if let Some(context) = context {
217:         record.set_context(context.display().to_string());
218:     }
219:     mutation.set_active(&record)
220: }
221: 
222: /// Post-commit maintenance: staging pointer cleanup, old-release pruning, and
223: /// temporary build context removal. All operate on the committed release, so
224: /// their failures never affect serving traffic.
225: fn run_maintenance(mutation: &SiteMutation, context_dir: &Path) -> Result<()> {
226:     stage("Pruning old releases");
227:     mutation.clear_staged_release()?;
228:     release::prune::run_locked(mutation, mutation.config().releases_keep)?;
229:     stage("Cleaning up");
230:     cleanup(mutation, Some(context_dir))
231: }
232: 
233: /// Records a post-commit maintenance failure as observable `cleanup_pending`
234: /// state: the new release is already serving, so the deployment itself did not
235: /// fail. The residual record keeps the site serialization-idle (a next
236: /// deployment may proceed and finish cleanup).
237: fn finish_cleanup_pending(mutation: &SiteMutation, context: Option<&Path>, error: &Error) {
238:     let site = mutation.site();
239:     let _ = cleanup(mutation, context);
240:     if let Ok(active) = mutation.active() {
241:         if let Some(mut record) = active {
242:             record.set_phase(release_state::DeploymentPhase::CleanupPending);
243:             record.set_error(error.to_string());
244:             let _ = mutation.set_active(&record);
245:         }
246:     }
247:     eprintln!(
248:         "Warning: the new release is active, but post-deploy maintenance was incomplete:\n  {error:#}\n  Run 'bonesremote release list --site {site}' to inspect. The residual state does not block future deployments and is cleared by the next successful deploy."
249:     );
250: }
251: 
252: fn stage(name: &str) {
253:     println!("{} {}", ansi("1;36", "->"), ansi("2", &format!("{name}...")));
254: }
255: 
256: fn ansi(code: &str, value: &str) -> String {
257:     format!("\x1b[{code}m{value}\x1b[0m")
258: }
259: 
260: fn finish_failed_activation(
261:     mutation: &SiteMutation,
262:     previous_release: &Path,
263:     context: Option<&Path>,
264:     error: Error,
265: ) -> Result<()> {
266:     let project_root = &mutation.config().project_root;
267:     if let Err(restore_error) = restore_previous_release(Path::new(project_root), previous_release) {
268:         return finish_abort_without_release_drop(
269:             mutation,
270:             context,
271:             error.context(format!("Failed to restore previous release: {restore_error:#}")),
272:         );
273:     }
274: 
275:     let error = match service::run_for_release(mutation) {
276:         Ok(()) => error,
277:         Err(restart_error) => error.context(format!("Failed to restart the restored release: {restart_error:#}")),
278:     };
279:     finish_abort(mutation, context, error)
280: }
281: 
282: pub fn restore_previous_release(project_root: &Path, previous_release: &Path) -> Result<()> {
283:     let current_link = PathBuf::from(project_root).join(paths::CURRENT_LINK);
284:     release_state::point_symlink_atomically(&current_link, previous_release)
285: }
286: 
287: fn process_start_ticks() -> Result<u64> {
288:     release::list::current_process_start_ticks().context("Failed to read deployment process start time")
289: }
290: 
291: fn deployment_started_at() -> Result<String> {
292:     static TIMESTAMP_FORMAT: &[FormatItem<'static>] =
293:         format_description!("[year]-[month]-[day]T[hour]:[minute]:[second]Z");
294:     OffsetDateTime::now_utc().format(TIMESTAMP_FORMAT).context("Failed to format deployment start time")
295: }
296: 
297: fn cleanup(mutation: &SiteMutation, context: Option<&Path>) -> Result<()> {
298:     if let Some(context) = context {
299:         lifecycle::checkout::cleanup_build_context(mutation.site(), context)?;
300:     }
301:     Ok(())
302: }
303: 
304: fn abort(mutation: &SiteMutation, context: Option<&Path>, error: Error) -> Result<()> {
305:     let mut error = abort_context_only(mutation, context, error);
306:     if let Err(drop_error) = drop_failed_release::run_locked(mutation) {
307:         error = error.context(format!("Failed to remove failed release: {drop_error:#}"));
308:     }
309:     Err(error)
310: }
311: 
312: fn finish_abort<T>(mutation: &SiteMutation, context: Option<&Path>, error: Error) -> Result<T> {
313:     let result = abort(mutation, context, error);
314:     match clear_active_after_result(mutation, result) {
315:         Ok(()) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!("Deployment abort unexpectedly succeeded")),
316:         Err(error) => Err(error),
317:     }
318: }
319: 
320: fn finish_abort_without_release_drop(mutation: &SiteMutation, context: Option<&Path>, error: Error) -> Result<()> {
321:     let error = abort_context_only(mutation, context, error);
322:     clear_active_after_result(mutation, Err(error))
323: }
324: 
325: fn clear_active_after_result(mutation: &SiteMutation, result: Result<()>) -> Result<()> {
326:     if let Err(clear_error) = mutation.clear_active() {
327:         return result
328:             .map_err(|error| error.context(format!("Failed to clear active deployment state: {clear_error:#}")));
329:     }
330:     result
331: }
332: 
333: fn abort_context_only(mutation: &SiteMutation, context: Option<&Path>, mut error: Error) -> Error {
334:     if let Err(cleanup_error) = cleanup(mutation, context) {
335:         error = error.context(format!("Cleanup failed: {cleanup_error:#}"));
336:     }
337:     error
338: }

20: pub fn run(site: &str, release: &str) -> Result<()> {
21:     privileges::ensure_root("bonesremote release kill")?;
22: 
23:     // A live deployment holds the site's lock, so cancellation must verify the
24:     // site identity and stop the process *before* the lock becomes available.
25:     // Only then is the guard assembled and used for all file mutations.
26:     validate_site_name(site)?;
27:     let config = Bones::for_site(site);
28:     let active = release_state::read_active_deployment(site)?;
29:     if let Some(active) = &active {
30:         if active.release() != release {
31:             bail!(
32:                 "Release {release} is not the active deployment. Run 'bonesdeploy site releases' to inspect releases."
33:             );
34:         }
35:         if active.phase().may_have_mutated_runtime() && list::process_matches(active) {
36:             bail!(
37:                 "Release {release} is preparing and cannot be cancelled because prepare scripts may change runtime state."
38:             );
39:         }
40:         if list::process_matches(active) {
41:             terminate_deployment(active)?;
42:         }
43:     } else if release_state::read_staged_release(site).ok().as_deref() != Some(release) {
44:         bail!("Release {release} is not building or interrupted. Run 'bonesdeploy site releases' to inspect releases.");
45:     }
46: 
47:     let lock = DeploymentLock::acquire(site)?;
48:     let mutation = SiteMutation::adopt(site, config.clone(), lock);
49:     let current = mutation.active()?;
50:     if current.as_ref().is_some_and(|deployment| deployment.release() != release) {
51:         bail!("Active deployment changed while cancelling {release}; no cleanup was performed.");
52:     }
53: 
54:     let build_user = build_user_for(site);
55:     let working_dir = Path::new(&config.project_root);
56:     ensure_build_user_ready(&build_user, working_dir)?;
57:     remove_build_container(&build_user, site, working_dir)?;
58: 
59:     if let Some(context) = current.as_ref().and_then(|deployment| deployment.context()) {
60:         let context = Path::new(context);
61:         let tmp_root = Path::new(&config.project_root).join(paths::TMP_BUILDS_DIR);
62:         if !context.starts_with(&tmp_root)
63:             || !context.file_name().is_some_and(|name| name.to_string_lossy().starts_with(&format!("build-{site}-")))
64:         {
65:             bail!("Refusing to remove invalid build context recorded for release {release}: {}", context.display());
66:         }
67:         checkout::cleanup_build_context(site, context)?;
68:     } else {
69:         cleanup_stale_contexts(site, &config.project_root)?;
70:     }
71: 
72:     let staged = mutation.staged_release()?;
73:     if staged.as_deref() == Some(release) {
74:         drop_failed_release::run_locked(&mutation)?;
75:     }
76:     mutation.clear_active()?;
77:     println!("Cancelled release: {release}");
78:     Ok(())
79: }

81: fn cleanup_stale_contexts(site: &str, project_root: &str) -> Result<()> {
82:     let tmp_root = Path::new(project_root).join(paths::TMP_BUILDS_DIR);
83:     if !tmp_root.is_dir() {
84:         return Ok(());

12: #[derive(Serialize)]

17: #[derive(Serialize)]

27: pub fn run(site: &str) -> Result<()> {
28:     privileges::ensure_root("bonesremote release list")?;
29:     validate_site_name(site)?;
30:     // Listing must remain available while deploy owns the mutation lock, so it
31:     // intentionally uses lock-free inspection with site-derived paths.
32:     let project_root = paths::default_project_root_for(site);
33:     let current = release_state::current_release_name(&project_root).ok();
34:     let active = release_state::read_active_deployment(site)?;
35:     let staged = release_state::read_staged_release(site).ok();
36:     let mut releases = release_state::list_releases_sorted(&project_root)?
37:         .into_iter()
38:         .map(|name| release(&name, current.as_deref(), active.as_ref(), staged.as_deref()))
39:         .collect::<Vec<_>>();
40:     releases.sort_by(|left, right| right.name.cmp(&left.name));
41: 
42:     println!("{}", serde_json::to_string(&Report { releases })?);
43:     Ok(())
44: }
45: 
46: fn release(name: &str, current: Option<&str>, active: Option<&DeploymentRecord>, staged: Option<&str>) -> Release {
47:     if current == Some(name) {
48:         return Release { name: name.to_string(), status: String::from("active"), phase: None, started_at: None };
49:     }
50: 
51:     if let Some(active) = active.filter(|active| active.release() == name) {
52:         let running = process_matches(active);
53:         return Release {
54:             name: name.to_string(),
55:             status: if running { phase_status(active.phase()) } else { String::from("interrupted") },
56:             phase: Some(active.phase().clone()),
57:             started_at: Some(active.started_at().to_string()),
58:         };
59:     }
60: 
61:     if staged == Some(name) {
62:         return Release { name: name.to_string(), status: String::from("interrupted"), phase: None, started_at: None };
63:     }
64: 
65:     Release { name: name.to_string(), status: String::from("previous"), phase: None, started_at: None }
66: }

68: fn phase_status(phase: &DeploymentPhase) -> String {
69:     match phase {
70:         DeploymentPhase::Created => String::from("created"),
71:         DeploymentPhase::SourceExported => String::from("source_exported"),
72:         DeploymentPhase::Built => String::from("built"),
73:         DeploymentPhase::Promoted => String::from("promoted"),
74:         DeploymentPhase::Prepared => String::from("prepared"),
75:         DeploymentPhase::Sealed => String::from("sealed"),
76:         DeploymentPhase::Activated => String::from("activated"),
77:         DeploymentPhase::Verified => String::from("verified"),
78:         DeploymentPhase::Completed => String::from("completed"),
79:         DeploymentPhase::CleanupPending => String::from("cleanup_pending"),
80:         DeploymentPhase::Failed => String::from("failed"),
81:     }
82: }
83: 
84: pub fn process_matches(active: &DeploymentRecord) -> bool {
85:     let stat = Path::new("/proc").join(active.pid().to_string()).join("stat");
86:     fs::read_to_string(stat)
87:         .ok()
88:         .and_then(|content| process_start_ticks(&content))
89:         .is_some_and(|ticks| ticks == active.process_start_ticks())
90: }
91: 
92: pub fn process_start_ticks(stat: &str) -> Option<u64> {
93:     let (_, fields) = stat.rsplit_once(") ")?;
94:     fields.split_whitespace().nth(19)?.parse().ok()
95: }
96: 
97: pub fn current_process_start_ticks() -> Option<u64> {
98:     let stat = fs::read_to_string(Path::new("/proc").join(process::id().to_string()).join("stat")).ok()?;
99:     process_start_ticks(&stat)
100: }

(End of file - total 100 lines)
</content>

57: 
58: Permissions are a provisioning-time contract, not a deployment-time repair. The ownership layout is established by `bonesdeploy server setup` and site setup, and never rewritten by deploy commands. If you find yourself wanting to `chmod` during a deploy, you are fixing the wrong thing — fix the provisioning. `shared/` is owned by the runtime user; only the app writes there. `releases/` is owned by the runtime user while prepare runs, then sealed as `root:<site>` before activation. The setgid bit on `releases/` lets the runtime group inherit read access without a post-deploy `chown`.
59: 
60: No shared groups with `660`/`770` everywhere — that pattern is a tangle of logic traps. No ACLs — they're opaque and unreadable. Ordinary Unix ownership, every time.
61: 
62: ## Privileged mediation
63: 
64: ```text
65: 13. BonesRemote accepts typed operations, not arbitrary root shell commands.
66: 14. Site names and release IDs are validated before path construction.
67: 15. All generated paths are constrained beneath canonical site roots.
68: 16. Symlinks are rejected or safely resolved in privileged write operations.
69: 17. Deployment is requested explicitly; no Git hook performs deployment work.
70: 18. User-controlled deployment input is never executed as root.
71: 19. Runtime users cannot modify configuration later consumed as code by root.
72: ```
73: 
74: BonesRemote is the privileged mediator. Its job is not to "run deployments" — its job is to constrain the deployer to a finite set of safe state transitions. It accepts narrow, typed operations like `activate_release(site="atlas", release="20260727_143200")`, never `run_as_root(command="...")` or `write_file(path="...", content="...")`.
75: 
76: Deployment is requested explicitly with `bonesdeploy deploy`. The application
77: revision supplies the source and its `infra/deployment` scripts; there is no
78: application Git hook, configuration repository, site import/export path, or
79: deploy-on-push trigger. The sudoers policy is rendered and validated by
80: BonesInfra at provisioning time with anchored site and revision arguments, so
81: trailing or malformed arguments are denied.

430: ## Runtime Identity Model
431: 
432: The current model uses a single per-project identity:
433: 
434: - **Runtime user**: `<site>` (system user, nologin, no home)
435: - **Runtime group**: `<site>`
436: - Releases are owned/sealed using the runtime group
437: - Directories: `releases/` is `root:runtime_group 2750`, `shared/` is `runtime_user:runtime_group 0750`
438: - The deploy user (`git`) is NOT added to the runtime group
439: 
440: ## Sudoers Contract
441: 
442: The deploy user can run only these narrow commands via sudo:
443: 
444: ```
445: bonesremote hook post-receive --site *
446: bonesremote service restart --site *
447: bonesremote release rollback --site *
448: bonesremote release drop-failed --site *
449: bonesremote release prune --site *
450: ```
451: 
452: The hook command itself owns the privileged deploy orchestration. No broad `bonesremote deploy --site *` sudo is granted.
453: 
454: ## Post-Receive Hook
455: 
456: A thin bash script at `<repo>/hooks/post-receive` derives the site name from `$GIT_DIR` and delegates:
457: 
458: ```bash
459: exec sudo bonesremote hook post-receive --site "$SITE"
460: ```
461: 
462: Branch filtering and deploy policy belong in `bonesremote hook post-receive`, not in the shell hook.
463: 
464: Source code must be pushed to the configured deployment branch before deploy can succeed. The bare repo's default branch (HEAD) is set via `git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/<branch>` during provisioning.
465:

40: provisions via `bonesinfra` or triggers `bonesremote` over SSH.
41: 
42: **`bonesinfra`** — an embedded Python provisioning runtime. Its committed pure-
43: Python wheel is materialized as `infra/bonesinfra-<version>-py3-none-any.whl`, while managed templates
44: are materialized under `infra/templates/`; a project-scoped venv installs the
45: wheel and its dependencies. It uses `pyinfra` to provision
46: the remote server (users, packages, frameworks, databases, SSL, firewalls) and
47: owns *what gets installed* at provisioning time.
48: 
49: **`bonesremote`** — the server-side binary that runs as root on the deployment
50: host. Owns the release lifecycle: staging, building, promoting, sealing,
51: activating, rolling back, pruning. It is the sole mutator of per-site deployment
52: state. It never calls `bonesinfra`.
53: 
54: ## 2. Responsibility / Ownership Map
55: 
56: This is the heart of the document. If a responsibility is listed here, the named
57: owner is canonical. Bypassing it creates a competing abstraction.
58: 
59: | Responsibility | Owner | Reuse / extend | Do not |
60: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
61: | Deployment configuration | `Bones` (`bonesdeploy-core`), loaded from root `.env` | Extend the canonical config model via `Runtime.extra` | Invent parallel config structs in either binary or Python |
62: | Product filesystem layout | `paths` / `DeploymentPaths` | Add path constants here | Scatter path literals in commands, templates, or scripts |
63: | Framework-specific config questions | Framework Rust module (`frameworks/<fw>.rs`) | Add sibling module + register in `frameworks.rs` | Inline prompt logic in init command |
64: | Framework provisioning | Installed BonesInfra wheel + `infra/templates` + `infra/custom`, loaded by `bonesinfra.project` | Extend managed framework or project-owned custom content | Special-case framework behavior in setup/runtime commands |
65: | Language runtime installation | `LanguageRuntime` ABC | Add subclass in `services/languages/` | Install runtimes directly from framework `runtime.py` |
66: | Database / server service provisioning | `RuntimeService` ABC + `SERVICE` registry | Add subclass + register in `SERVICE` dict | Put DB provisioning in framework code |
67: | Remote site mutation | `SiteMutation` | Acquire it before any site state change | Create independent locking or config-validation paths |

<skill_content name="code-reviewer">
# Skill: code-reviewer

# Code Reviewer

Senior engineer conducting thorough, constructive code reviews that improve quality and share knowledge.

## When to Use This Skill

- Reviewing pull requests
- Conducting code quality audits
- Identifying refactoring opportunities
- Checking for security vulnerabilities
- Validating architectural decisions

## Core Workflow

1. **Context** — Read PR description, understand the problem being solved. **Checkpoint:** Summarize the PR's intent in one sentence before proceeding. If you cannot, ask the author to clarify.
2. **Structure** — Review architecture and design decisions. Ask: Does this follow existing patterns in the codebase? Are new abstractions justified?
3. **Details** — Check code quality, security, and performance. Apply the checks in the Reference Guide below. Ask: Are there N+1 queries, hardcoded secrets, or injection risks?
4. **Tests** — Validate test coverage and quality. Ask: Are edge cases covered? Do tests assert behavior, not implementation?
5. **Feedback** — Produce a categorized report using the Output Template. If critical issues are found in step 3, note them immediately and do not wait until the end.

> **Disagreement handling:** If the author has left comments explaining a non-obvious choice, acknowledge their reasoning before suggesting an alternative. Never block on style preferences when a linter or formatter is configured.

## Reference Guide

Load detailed guidance based on context:

<!-- Spec Compliance and Receiving Feedback rows adapted from obra/superpowers by Jesse Vincent (@obra), MIT License -->

| Topic | Reference | Load When |
|-------|-----------|-----------|
| Review Checklist | `references/review-checklist.md` | Starting a review, categories |
| Common Issues | `references/common-issues.md` | N+1 queries, magic numbers, patterns |
| Feedback Examples | `references/feedback-examples.md` | Writing good feedback |
| Report Template | `references/report-template.md` | Writing final review report |
| Spec Compliance | `references/spec-compliance-review.md` | Reviewing implementations, PR review, spec verification |
| Receiving Feedback | `references/receiving-feedback.md` | Responding to review comments, handling feedback |

## Review Patterns (Quick Reference)

### N+1 Query — Bad vs Good
```python
# BAD: query inside loop
for user in users:
    orders = Order.objects.filter(user=user)  # N+1

# GOOD: prefetch in bulk
users = User.objects.prefetch_related('orders').all()
```

### Magic Number — Bad vs Good
```python
# BAD
if status == 3:
    ...

# GOOD
ORDER_STATUS_SHIPPED = 3
if status == ORDER_STATUS_SHIPPED:
    ...
```

### Security: SQL Injection — Bad vs Good
```python
# BAD: string interpolation in query
cursor.execute(f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {user_id}")

# GOOD: parameterized query
cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s", [user_id])
```

## Constraints

### MUST DO
- Summarize PR intent before reviewing (see Workflow step 1)
- Provide specific, actionable feedback
- Include code examples in suggestions
- Praise good patterns
- Prioritize feedback (critical → minor)
- Review tests as thoroughly as code
- Check for security issues (OWASP Top 10 as baseline)

### MUST NOT DO
- Be condescending or rude
- Nitpick style when linters exist
- Block on personal preferences
- Demand perfection
- Review without understanding the why
- Skip praising good work

## Output Template

Code review report must include:
1. **Summary** — One-sentence intent recap + overall assessment
2. **Critical issues** — Must fix before merge (bugs, security, data loss)
3. **Major issues** — Should fix (performance, design, maintainability)
4. **Minor issues** — Nice to have (naming, readability)
5. **Positive feedback** — Specific patterns done well
6. **Questions for author** — Clarifications needed
7. **Verdict** — Approve / Request Changes / Comment

## Knowledge Reference

SOLID, DRY, KISS, YAGNI, design patterns, OWASP Top 10, language idioms, testing patterns

<task id="ses_fafcdf1abffe3mtriiG4Zq0C3l" state="completed">
<task_result>
# Review: `fix/gitdeploy` worktree (uncommitted changes)

Bottom line: this is a partial implementation of the plan (`docs/plans/fix/gitdeploy/03-tasks.md:21-25` admits the lifecycle split, sudoers expansion, and migration are unfinished). As diffed, **deployment is non-operational in both the new git-mode and the old root-mode**, and there are concrete permission/secret regressions. Findings in priority order:

---

## P0 — Deployment is broken

### 1. `sudo -n bonesremote config sync` is denied by sudoers
- `crates/bonesdeploy/src/infra/mod.rs:27-29` — the new sync command runs under `sudo -n` as `git`.
- `crates/bonesinfra/python/src/bonesinfra/assets/sudoers/bonesdeploy.j2:16` — the allowlist is byte-identical to `develop` (only comments changed): `service restart`, `release rollback`, `release drop-failed`, `release prune`. There is **no `config sync` rule**.
- With `-n`, sudo fails immediately, so `bonesdeploy deploy` dies at the first remote step on every provisioned host. (Previously the root session ran `config sync` directly; sudo was never needed.) When adding the rule, note the anchored regexes must match the full argv including the trailing `--config-stdin`.

### 2. The synchronized snapshot is unreadable by `git`
- `crates/bonesremote/src/control_plane.rs:68-71` — `store()` (running as root via sudo) does `fs::create_dir_all(parent)` for `/var/lib/bonesdeploy/config/<site>` and sets mode `0750`, but never chgrp's it. The directory is created **root:root**, and `git` (not in group `root`) cannot traverse it.
- Provisioning doesn't cover it either: `snapshot_root` was added to `DeploymentPaths` (`crates/bonesinfra/python/src/bonesinfra/config/paths.py:114,182`) but no mkdir uses it; only the parent root is provisioned `root:git 0750` (`server/__init__.py:60-66`).
- Consequence: even with the sudoers fixed, `control_plane::load` (`control_plane.rs:94-102`) fails with PermissionDenied → deploy cannot start. The 0644 file mode (line 81) is irrelevant behind an untraversable dir.

### 3. The lifecycle still hard-requires root; there is no elevation mechanism
`run_full` dropped the root gate (`crates/bonesremote/src/commands/deploy/lifecycle.rs:15-29`), but the coordinator then calls in-process root-only steps, and nothing in `crates/bonesremote/src` ever execs `sudo`:
- `lifecycle.rs:23` → `ensure_build_user_ready` runs `systemctl start user@<uid>.service` and `systemd-run --machine=<user>@` (`crates/bonesremote/src/release/lifecycle/build/build_user.rs:51-54, 63-69`) — fails as `git` before anything else.
- `stage.rs:22`, `checkout.rs:18`, `build/mod.rs:19,24,29`, `wire_shared.rs:12`, `prepare.rs:29`, `activate.rs:11`, `service.rs:22-23` (via `run_for_release`, coordinator.rs:173) — all `ensure_root`.
- Even ignoring the checks, the filesystem is root-controlled: `releases/` is `root:<runtime-group> 2750` (`directories.py:66-72`), project root `root:root 0751` (`directories.py:58-64`), and the build context is created at `/srv/sites/<site>/tmp` (`checkout.rs:13-15, 53-59`) — `git` has no write access. Abort/maintenance paths (`drop_failed_release::run_locked` coordinator.rs:306, `prune::run_locked` coordinator.rs:228) delete inside `releases/` and fail as git.
- The sudoers has no rules for any lifecycle transition, so there is nothing for the coordinator to call even if it shelled out.

Net: git-mode fails at step one; the old root-mode fails because `deploy --config-stdin` was removed (`args.rs`, `dispatch.rs:11`) and `bonesdeploy deploy` no longer connects as root (`commands/deploy.rs:27-30`). Both models are broken simultaneously.

---

## P1 — Regressions and contract violations

### 4. Borg passphrase split-brain: backups break, or the secret moves into git-owned space
- Reader moved with the state root: `bonesremote_site_passphrase_path` → `/var/lib/bonesdeploy/state/<site>/.borg_passphrase` (`crates/bonesdeploy-core/src/paths.rs:125-127, 150-152`), read by `bonesremote backup run` (`crates/bonesremote/src/commands/backup.rs:28, 72-82`).
- Provisioner unchanged: BonesInfra still writes the passphrase to `/root/.config/bonesremote/sites/<site>/.borg_passphrase` (`crates/bonesinfra/python/src/bonesinfra/config/paths.py:219`; `services/linux/backup.py:32, 38, 66`).
- Result: after re-provisioning, `bonesremote backup run` fails "Missing Borg passphrase". And if provisioning is naively "fixed" to the new path, the secret lands under a `git:git 0700` tree (`server/__init__.py:53-59`) — handing the deploy identity the backup passphrase, violating `docs/security/invariants.md:51-53`. The passphrase must stay root-only; do not derive it from the new state root.

### 5. Lock provisioning contradicts its own threat model
- Locks root is `root:git 0770` (`server/__init__.py:67-73`). A group-writable directory means `git` can unlink/recreate `.&#8203;<site>.deployment.lock`, defeating the plan's stated property "git can lock it but cannot replace the lock inode" (`docs/plans/fix/gitdeploy/02-plan.md:20-22`). `0750` would suffice for opening the pre-created `0660` file (`directories.py:24-28`).
- `DeploymentLock::acquire` (`crates/bonesremote/src/release/state/mod.rs:69-82`) does `create_dir_all` + `OpenOptions::create(true)`: on a host not re-provisioned since upgrade, `git` either fails to create `/var/lib/bonesdeploy/locks` (root-owned parent) or silently creates a git-owned lock — the root-pinned lock then protects nothing. Not privilege escalation, but a compromised `git` key can defeat deployment mutual exclusion.

### 6. No legacy state migration — upgraded hosts lose deployment state
- State moved from `/root/.config/bonesremote/sites/<site>` (root:root 0700) to `/var/lib/bonesdeploy/state/<site>` (git:git 0700): `crates/bonesdeploy-core/src/paths.rs:61, 120-122`; `server/__init__.py:53-59`; `directories.py:16-22`.
- `migrate_previous` (`crates/bonesremote/src/release/state/store.rs:78-121`) only migrates legacy file *formats* within the new root; nothing relocates state from the old root (which git cannot read anyway).
- Consequences: `release list`/`status`/idle checks see empty state; an in-flight `active` record at upgrade time is dropped, so `ensure_site_idle` (`commands/mod.rs:18-30`) permits concurrent deploys; old files are orphaned under `/root`. `03-tasks.md` admits this is unfinished; it must land (as a root-run migration step) before this ships.

---

## P2 — Consistency issues with real consequences

### 7. Sudoers entries no longer match any invocation path
The four allowed commands (`bonesdeploy.j2:16`) are now invoked only in-process by the coordinator or directly as root (`crates/bonesdeploy/src/commands/rollback.rs:23`, `site/status.rs:85`, `site/releases.rs:74,86` use `connect_privileged`); the post-receive hook that consumed them is removed from the docs/model. Meanwhile the one command that *does* need sudo is missing (P0-1). The final allowlist should be derived from the actual typed-transition invocations, or it is dead policy that looks like protection.

### 8. Documentation now states wrong paths/claims (operator-facing, not style)
- `CONTEXT.md:238-239` — site doctor still documented as syncing/reading `/srv/conf/<site>/bones.json` and state under `/root/.config/...`; actual snapshot is `/var/lib/bonesdeploy/config/<site>/bones.json` (`control_plane.rs:33-37, 56-61`).
- `CONTEXT.md:155` — passphrase documented at the provisioning path, contradicting the new reader path (P1-4).
- `README.md:419`, `docs/architecture/reference.md:721-722`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:605-608` — still describe the deploy `--config-stdin` descriptor and `/srv/conf/<site>/bones.json`.
- `docs/security/invariants.md:47-48` (invariant 10 "Root owns … deployment state") and `:51-53` (root owns the passphrase) now conflict with the implementation: state is git-owned, and the passphrase implicitly would be. Invariants and code must agree before merge.

---

## P3 — Minor
- `crates/bonesdeploy-core/src/paths.rs:165-173` — `bonesremote_sites_root_resolved()` (env `BONESREMOTE_SITES_ROOT`) has no callers left; the only override consumer is the thread-local in `state/mod.rs:57-64`. Dead code left behind by the change.
- `server/__init__.py:41-52` still provisions `/root/.config/bonesremote` + `sites/`; remaining consumers are the doctor baseline check (`commands/doctor/baseline.rs:15`) and the legacy passphrase path — should be resolved together with P1-4/P1-6.
- `crates/bonesremote/tests/cli.rs:31-35` — `deploy_accepts_a_site_without_a_config_descriptor` only asserts exit ≠ 2; it passes for any non-clap failure and depends on no snapshot existing at the real system path on the test host. The second new test (`:37-40`) is fine.

## What is correct
- Removing the second descriptor path (`deploy` no longer accepts `--config-stdin`) closes the config-bypass hole the plan targets; the coordinator now reads only the root-synced snapshot.
- `sync_control_plane_command` properly quotes the site (`ssh.rs:35-37`), and `config sync` remains root-only with site validation (`commands/config.rs:6`, `control_plane.rs:63-66`) — safe to allowlist once the rule exists.
- Lock/state path derivation keeps the test override semantics, and the wheel was regenerated with the new Python (`BONESREMOTE_STATE_ROOT`/`LOCK_ROOT`/`DEPLOYMENT_SNAPSHOT_ROOT` verified inside `bonesinfra-0.3.4-py3-none-any.whl`).

**Recommendation:** do not merge as-is. Minimum to restore operation: (a) add the anchored `config sync` sudoers rule, (b) fix `store()` to chgrp/chown the per-site snapshot dir to `git`, (c) either complete the typed privileged-transition split with sudoers + filesystem changes, or revert the entrypoint/root-gate changes until it exists; and resolve P1-4 (passphrase), P1-5 (lock dir mode), P1-6 (migration) before touching production hosts.

## Assistant (Plan · GPT-5.6 Sol · 25.0s)

_Thinking:_

**Identifying server doctor root ownership issue**

_Thinking:_

**Citing precise code references for review**

**Critical Issues**
1. `bonesdeploy deploy` is immediately denied by sudoers.  
   `crates/bonesdeploy/src/infra/mod.rs:17-20` runs `sudo -n bonesremote config sync`, but `crates/bonesinfra/python/src/bonesinfra/assets/sudoers/bonesdeploy.j2:16` does not allow `config sync`. Every deployment therefore fails before coordination begins.

2. The synchronized snapshot is unreadable by `git`.  
   `crates/bonesremote/src/control_plane.rs:63-82` creates `/var/lib/bonesdeploy/config/<site>` as root and only changes its mode to `0750`; it never assigns group `git`. Provisioning creates only the parent as `root:git` (`server/__init__.py:60-66`). The resulting per-site directory is `root:root 0750`, so `control_plane::load()` cannot traverse it as `git`.

3. The coordinator still invokes root-only lifecycle operations in-process.  
   Removing `ensure_root` from `commands/deploy/lifecycle.rs:15` does not make deployment unprivileged. It immediately calls privileged systemd work at `lifecycle.rs:23`, followed by phases that still reject non-root callers:
   - `release/lifecycle/stage.rs:22`
   - `checkout.rs:18`
   - `build/mod.rs:19-29`
   - `wire_shared.rs:12`
   - `prepare.rs:29`
   - `activate.rs:11`

   No typed helper commands or matching sudoers rules exist yet. Consequently the new `git` deployment path cannot complete.

**Major Issues**
4. Moving `bonesremote_sites_root()` also moved the Borg passphrase lookup into git-owned state.  
   `paths.rs:120-151` now derives `.borg_passphrase` under `/var/lib/bonesdeploy/state/<site>`, while provisioning still writes it under `/root/.config/bonesremote/sites/<site>` (`services/linux/backup.py:30-42`). Backups will report a missing passphrase. Moving the provisioned secret to the new path would expose it beneath a `git:git` directory, violating the intended secret boundary.

5. The lock directory permits `git` to replace lock files.  
   `server/__init__.py:67-72` provisions `/var/lib/bonesdeploy/locks` as `root:git 0770`. Group write authority lets `git` unlink and replace the supposedly root-pinned lock inode. Additionally, `DeploymentLock::acquire()` still uses `create(true)` at `release/state/mod.rs:69-82`, allowing an unprovisioned lock to be created with the wrong ownership.

6. Existing deployment state is not migrated.  
   `store.rs:78-120` only migrates old file formats within the newly selected state root. It never relocates state from `/root/.config/bonesremote/sites/<site>`. After upgrading, active or interrupted deployment records appear absent, potentially allowing a conflicting deployment.

7. Server doctor now rejects the provisioned state root.  
   `commands/doctor/baseline.rs:16` requires `bonesremote_sites_root()` to be root-owned, but that function now returns `/var/lib/bonesdeploy/state`, which provisioning deliberately owns as `git:git`. Server doctor will report a baseline failure on correctly provisioned hosts.

8. The tests prove CLI parsing, not deploy operability.  
   `crates/bonesremote/tests/cli.rs:29-34` only checks that deploy does not exit with Clap status `2`; any runtime failure passes. There is no test connecting the config-sync sudoers rule, snapshot ownership, lock ownership, and lifecycle invocation contract.

**Positive Notes**
- Removing the second deploy descriptor closes the configuration-bypass path.
- Site arguments remain shell-quoted and validated.
- The snapshot, state, and lock concepts are being separated in the right general direction.
- Formatting, linting, and unit suites pass, but they do not exercise these host-level permission boundaries.

**Verdict**
Request changes. The branch is explicitly partial and currently leaves deployments and backups non-operational; it should not be merged until the typed privileged lifecycle, sudoers contract, ownership setup, and migration are completed together.
